reviews.review: The controls are horrible.  Some might like it though.

Tough game to recommend, if you can even consider that. It is a “souls-like” with guns that suffers from lack of polish and numerous bugs or glitches. I gave the game a fair shot and completed a full playthrough but it took me some effort to do so as the core gameplay becomes repetitive within first hour and doesn’t get much better later on. 

There’s a lot of odd design decisions that make combat more frustrating than fun, for example there are snipers that can teleport and shoot you from behind within less than 1 second, every ~5th enemy also has some sort of bulletproof shield that forces you to to flank them or aim for barely exposed head or feet. It wouldn’t be a problem in itself if they didn’t spawn in narrow corridors or had 2-3 earlier mentioned snipers to back them up. There’s also zombies with broken melee hitboxes (you get hit even if you stand 1.5m away from them), exploding enemies spawning from the ground around you (etc.), the just just goes on. And since you fight groups of them 80% of the time there’s no reason to use other weapon than a sniper rifle that can hit most targets beyond their engagement range. 

Core game progression focuses on improving your stats in order to equip weapons with better stats, there isn’t much else to that. Most weapons do have some special abilities that require energy to use (mana-equivalent) but except grenade launcher, they’re all rather weak and long charge-up time before each shot made me simply not use them for majority of the game.

The entire game is rather forgettable from story to gameplay and its art direction, its like the developers took inspiration from Dark Souls games in but didn’t fully understand them. I don’t want to sound like I’m picking on the game too much but its actually difficult for me to think of any positives about Immortal: Unchained other than that it didn't crash in my 15h while playing it

I can’t think of a situation where I’d recommend this game for someone over any other similar souls-like shooters out there. So yeah, even if you’re a fan of the genre I recommend skipping this game.
